alternatives: A real carton/object held, jammed, or continuously obstructing the entry location while the belt moves underneath or past it cannot be excluded from these signals alone.
The observations do not directly inspect the photoeye, its wiring/input path, or the physical entry location.
The encoder distance required for a carton to reach sensor.d1Approach is not supplied, so absent downstream activation alone is less decisive than entry never clearing.

finalDiagnosis.explanation: The diagnosis is updated away from an ordinary real stationary carton and toward an entry indication that remains stuck true. Belt motion was proven: encoder rose from 0 in OBS-004 through 12 in OBS-013 to 842 in OBS-030 and 1842 in OBS-051, belt speed reached 0.5, and running feedback was true. Throughout that proven motion, sensor.entry remained true and d1Approach, d2Approach, exitA, exitB, and runout remained false, e.g. OBS-013, OBS-030, and OBS-051. After stopping, encoder settled at 1900 with speed 0 in OBS-055 and OBS-057, yet entry remained true and all downstream sensors remained false. That pattern supports entry_sensor_stuck_true, but physical inspection is not available, so a carton/object physically held at entry or another entry-path cause is not ruled out.

uncertaintyReduction.explanation: Confidence in the leading stuck-true entry hypothesis increased because the bounded run discriminated the original alternatives: the drive and belt did move, proven by encoder, belt speed, and running feedback in OBS-013, OBS-030, and OBS-051, yet entry never cleared and no downstream sensor activated in those same observations. The stopped final state in OBS-055 and OBS-057 preserved the same entry-true/downstream-false pattern. Uncertainty remains because no direct physical or sensor-path inspection was observed and a held/jammed object at entry could produce similar signals.
